note: FNS 1161.1 is QC error determination methodology — it instructs reviewers how to calculate variances when households failed to report expenses at certification. The core rule ('reviewer will determine the error by using the amount of the expense at the time of certification') and the prorating instruction for periodic/annual expenses are QC audit procedures, not caseworker policy. The one policy-relevant element — the disclaimer/forfeiture exception — is functionally implemented in Massachusetts: the OLG treats all expense deductions as optional verifications (Expenses/Deductions Introduction: 'Households that do not verify these expenses at application... cannot be denied or closed for failure to provide verifications' but 'the expense is not allowed and the benefit and eligibility amount is calculated without the expense'). Households are informed via VC-1 that unverified expenses won't be credited, which constitutes the disclaimer language FNS references. This forfeiture approach means unreported expenses at certification would not generate QC errors under FNS 1161.1's own exception clause, making the QC calculation methodology moot for Massachusetts cases where the VC-1 process was followed.
